claims.text: Teratogenic and retained in the body: not for pregnant patients or anyone who may become pregnant, who must avoid pregnancy for at least 3 years after stopping. Long-term use may cause diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis (DISH)
claims.quote: Because of the teratogenic potential and long-term retention of acitretin in the body, it should not be used in pregnant patients or those with child bearing potential; such patients should also be warned against becoming pregnant for at least 3 years after treatment ends. Pregnancy restrictions also apply to isotretinoin, but the agent is not retained in the body beyond 1 month. Long-term treatment may be associated with diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis (DISH).

claims.text: Acitretin for 9 to 12 months has been effective in some patients
claims.quote: Oral retinoids (isotretinoin for 4 to 6 months or acitretin for 9 to 12 months) have been effective in some patients (7).
